espn-604011.headline: Fiji again, and this time the loser finishes last
beats: Fiji won 21–16 in Udine on 21 November. The rematch is the 11th-place final at Allianz Stadium, and whoever loses ends the inaugural Nations Championship at the bottom.

Italy have lost seven straight, the last two to Argentina and Fiji by five points each. Gonzalo Quesada says they built the conditions to win in both and did not finish the job. Win by 16 or more and Italy go above Fiji to 10th in the world.

He has made five changes. Niccolò Cannone takes the captaincy from Giacomo Nicotera, who led Italy in Udine and now starts on the bench. Enoch Opoku-Gyamfi makes his first Test start at No 8. Jake White has changed Fiji's entire front row and both half-backs from the side that won.
Italy's next Test is at Scotland in February. Fiji's is Spain at the 2027 World Cup. The loser has a long time to look at the table.

espn-604012.headline: Playing for fifth, with first in the world on offer
beats: This is the Nations Championship's fifth-place final. Beat Australia and Ireland go up to 1st in the world rankings, above South Africa, the side they edged 20–17 last week.
The last meeting, in Australia on 4 July, went 33–31 to Ireland. Australia have since conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October. They reached this game with a 29–26 win in Wales.

Andy Farrell has picked virtually the same side that beat the Springboks, with Jacob Stockdale recalled to the starting team. Australia lean on longer memories: Allan Alaalatoa co-captains on his 100th cap, and Kurtley Beale, 37, is on the bench four years after his last Test.
Ireland host England in the Six Nations on 6 February. Win here and they could do it as the world's top-ranked side, having spent the autumn qualifying for fifth.

espn-604013.headline: Japan let in 145 since Wales last edged them by seven
beats: Before England put 78 on Japan and Scotland 67, Wales beat them 28–21 on 7 November. Neither side has won this fixture by more than 10 points since Japan beat Wales 23–8 in 2013.

Wales have since beaten New Zealand 35–28, a first win over the All Blacks in 73 years, then lost 29–26 to Australia. James Botham, player of the match against New Zealand and left out of the 23 for Australia, is back in the side. Reuben Morgan-Williams makes his first Test start, and Dafydd Jenkins captains.

Eddie Jones has made nine changes to Japan's starting side, the third game running he has made a raft of them. A Japan win by 16 or more would take them above Wales in the world rankings, a margin this fixture has not produced for either side since 2013.
Wales go to France in February. Japan have nothing scheduled, so whatever happens here is the result they keep.

espn-604014.headline: Do it again by 16 and England are top of the world
beats: England beat New Zealand 37–12 at Allianz Stadium on 21 November, their biggest-ever win over them. Results elsewhere put the two sides into the third-place final on the same ground a week later.

New Zealand have lost to Wales, for the first time since 1953, and to England on successive weekends. They have made six changes. England have won five straight and changed five anyway, with Exeter back row Greg Fisilau making his first England start.
A win by 16 or more takes England top of the world rankings, above South Africa, Ireland and France. Last week's margin was 25.
Lose, and New Zealand's next game is at home to Chile at the World Cup in October 2027. That is a long time to think about Allianz Stadium.

espn-604015.headline: One win each, and the decider is in London
beats: Argentina won 33–24 in Scotland last November. Scotland answered 47–38 in Cordoba in July, finishing strongly after a debut try from hooker Gregor Hiddleston. Sunday's 7th-place final at Twickenham is fourth in the north against fourth in the south, and the third leg of a year that has gone one each.

Argentina arrive from a 45–17 loss in Paris that cost them more than the result. Replacement loose-head Mayco Vivas was sent off and is out, and Pablo Matera, a centurion, misses the game for personal reasons.

Scotland are short too. Matt Fagerson broke down with a jaw injury in the 67–5 win over Japan, with Jack Dempsey and Jamie Ritchie already injured. That leaves room for Liam McConnell, who scored a hat-trick in that game on his second Test start.
Argentina have won two Tests this year. A third by 16 points or more would take them above Scotland in the world rankings, into the 6th place Scotland have held since October.

espn-604016.headline: South Africa may repeat the start that left them 21–7 down
beats: Rassie Erasmus is expected to start his second-choice front row again in the Nations Championship final, barring a late change. In Paris on 13 November, the first-choice trio came on in the 35th minute with France 21–7 up. France did not score after the break and still won 21–19.
Nick Mallett's worry is the first half, not the second: "They are fast starters". His fix is for South Africa to hold the line for 40 minutes and let the bench make the statement.

France reach the final without the locks Emmanuel Meafou and Thibaud Flament. Fabien Galthié reckons "There's at least one team's worth of players missing, maybe even two." Thomas Ramos, who missed the Paris win, is set to return from a thigh issue.
South Africa have lost their last two, by two points and by three. A third would hand the world's top ranking to France, the side that started the run.
